sentences.text:
The present petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 482 Cr.PC seeking quashing of
the Fir No.0320/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 Ipc registered at Ps Ambedkar Nagar, Delhi
and the proceedings pursuant thereto, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.

3. Learned APP for the State submits that since the present FIR has arisen out of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have amicably settled all their disputes, the State has no objection in case the present FIR is quashed.
4. The petitioner (former husband) and the respondent no.2 (former wife) are present in the Court and they have been identified by their
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 09:15:38 respective counsels and the Investigating Officer, ASI Jagroop, PS Ambedkar Nagar, Delhi.
5. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the parties were solemnised on 29.08.2013 at Begusarai, Bihar as per the Muslim rites and ceremonies.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
6. However, on account of temperamental issues, certain disputes arose between the parties and they started living separately w.e.f. 05.08.2015.

sentences.text: The parties with the intervention of common friends entered into a settlement agreement on 17.01.2023.

In terms of the said settlement, the parties have agreed that a total sum of 3 lakhs and dowry articles containing one Hero Passion Bike, one small trunk, one bed, one dressing table shall be paid/returned by the petitioner to the respondent no.2.
8.
Insofar as the payment of 3 lakhs is concerned, the same was to be paid in three instalments.
Out of the said amount of 3 lakhs, an amount of 2 lakhs has already been paid, the receipt of which is acknowledged by the respondent no.2.

The balance amount of 1 lakh has been paid by the petitioner to the respondent no.2 today in the Court by way of a cheque bearing no.408876 dated 22.03.2023 drawn on State Bank of India, Khagaria Bazar, Thana Road, Khagaria, Khagaria District,
Bihar.
9.
The respondent no.2 states that she has no objection in receiving the payment by way of a cheque.
She, however, adds that quashing of the FIR may be made subject to encashment of the said cheque.

10. Learned counsel for the parties have drawn the attention of the Court to the affidavit of respondent no.2 wherein she has stated that the marriage between her and the petitioner has been dissolved mutually by way of decree of divorce through triple talaq in three notices.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 09:15:38 11.
On a query made by the Court to the respondent no2, she states that she has no objection in case the FIR is quashed.

12. In view of the fact that the parties have amicably settled their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would, therefore, be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings emanating there from.
13. There is also no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

Accordingly, subject to clearance of the aforesaid cheque, the FIR No.0320/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at PS Ambedkar Nagar, Delhi and all proceedings emanating there from are hereby quashed.
14. The petition is disposed of in the above terms.
15. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MAY 16, 2023 MK
